title: Adaptive Surrogate-Assisted Algorithm for Sensitivity Analysis and Therapeutic Regime Mapping in a CAR-T Cell Therapy Model
content: Spatiotemporal models of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy can clarify how interacting biological mechanisms shape therapeutic response, but global sensitivity analysis and response-regime mapping require many computationally expensive simulations. We developed an adaptive surrogate-assisted algorithm that combines these tasks within a single computational framework. Independent Gaussian process surrogates were constructed for the final and minimum normalised tumour burdens, and new simulations were selected according to surrogate uncertainty and proximity to regime boundaries. Surrogates trained on 120 simulations achieved normalised root-mean-square errors of 0.00148 and 0.01058 on a fully held-out test set. Regime classification agreed with direct simulations at all 30 test points and 12 additional points near regime boundaries. The stopping criterion was first satisfied after 84 training simulations, while the advantage of adaptive sampling was most evident at intermediate computational budgets. Antigen escape and cytotoxicity dominated the variance in final tumour burden, with total-order Sobol indices of 0.4944 and 0.4382, respectively. Chemotaxis contributed much less to global variance but shifted the boundary between partial response and regrowth. These results show that global sensitivity ranking and regime-boundary analysis provide complementary information and can be combined within a limited budget of direct full-model simulations.
